title: The Lost Book (മലയാളം)
summary: A fire destroys the imperial archive, burning a rare treatise on philosophy. Birbal comforts Akbar by demonstrating the permanence of internalized wisdom. [ML]
full_text:
A sudden fire in the library wing of the Agra palace destroyed dozens of precious illuminated manuscripts. Emperor Akbar was inconsolable over the loss of a unique, centuries-old Persian treatise on ethics and statecraft, which had been copied by master calligraphers and bound in gold leather.

Weeping with grief, Akbar said to Birbal: 'The greatest wisdom of the ancients is lost forever to the flames! Those words can never be replaced! The soul of our library has turned to ash!'

Birbal sat quietly beside the grieving monarch and said in a gentle, reassuring voice:

'Sire, fire has consumed only dried sheepskin, ink, and gold leaf. It has not burned a single grain of true wisdom.'

Akbar looked up, bewildered: 'How can you say that? The only copy in Hindustan was destroyed!'

Birbal explained:

'Your Majesty, a book is merely a wooden box that carries the fruit of knowledge. If a man reads a book and merely leaves the words on the shelf, the knowledge perishes when the paper burns.

'But if a ruler reads those words, reflects upon them in his heart, and practices justice, mercy, and compassion in his daily rule, then the book has migrated from the dead page into the living soul of the monarch!

'Can any fire burn the kindness you showed to the starving peasant yesterday? Can any ash erase the fair judgments you delivered from your throne? The words of that ancient author live on in your actions. As long as you practice righteousness, the book is alive in Hindustan!'

Akbar's heart found immediate comfort. Inspired by Birbal's words, the Emperor commissioned new scholars to compose fresh treatises based on living experience, realizing that wisdom's true temple is the human heart.
